topic.seo_description: Explore omega-3 fatty acids in cancer research. Discover latest peer-reviewed studies on prevention and treatment support benefits.
topic.seo_intro:
Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated fats found primarily in fatty fish, algae, and plant sources like flaxseed and walnuts. These essential nutrients have garnered significant attention in cancer research due to their potential anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. Unlike saturated fats, omega-3s—particularly EPA and DHA—work at the cellular level to support various biological processes that researchers believe may influence cancer risk and progression.

The scientific interest in omega-3 fatty acids stems from epidemiological studies showing associations between higher omega-3 intake and reduced cancer incidence in certain populations, as well as laboratory research demonstrating mechanisms by which these compounds may slow cancer cell growth and enhance the effectiveness of conventional treatments. While omega-3s are not considered a standalone cancer treatment, emerging evidence suggests they may play a complementary role in a comprehensive cancer care strategy, potentially helping to manage treatment side effects, support immune function, and reduce inflammation associated with cancer development.

The current state of omega-3 research in oncology includes clinical trials investigating optimal dosing, duration of supplementation, and efficacy in different cancer types. This page features the latest peer-reviewed studies, clinical trial results, and expert analyses examining how omega-3 fatty acids may support cancer prevention efforts and complement conventional treatment approaches. Whether you're exploring preventive strategies or seeking information about integrative options alongside medical treatment, the research below represents the most current scientific findings in this rapidly evolving field.

articles.title: Phase 2 Study of Low Dose Tamoxifen +/- High Dose Omega-3 Fatty Acids in Overweight Postmenopausal Women at Increased Risk for Breast Cancer
articles.hook: Low-dose tamoxifen and omega-3 reduce breast cancer risk
articles.summary: Researchers are testing whether low-dose tamoxifen, with or without omega-3 supplements, can reduce breast cancer risk in overweight postmenopausal women.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of the Effects of UNICLA-A2 Against Conventional Dairy Products Administered Daily in Patients at High-risk Colorectal Cancer Development Who Have Undergone Polypectomy
articles.hook: A2 milk with omega-3 and selenium reduces colorectal cancer recurrence risk
articles.summary: A specialized A2 milk product with omega-3 and selenium may help prevent colorectal cancer recurrence in high-risk polypectomy patients.

articles.title: Higher dietary omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid intake is associated with reduced all-cause mortality in cancer survivors: A prospective cohort study.
articles.hook: Omega-3 fatty acids associated with lower mortality in cancer survivors
articles.summary: Cancer survivors eating more omega-3 fatty acids show significantly lower death rates, especially if overweight or obese.

articles.title: Comparative Effect of African Walnut Oil and Docosahexaenoic Acid on Hematological and Oxidative Stress Markers of Female Wistar Rats With 7,12-Dimethylbenz[a]anthracene-Induced Breast Cancer.
articles.hook: African walnut oil reduces tumor size in breast cancer rats
articles.summary: African walnut oil reduced breast cancer tumor size and improved blood health markers and oxidative stress in rats.

articles.title: n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids Improve DSS-Induced Acute Colitis in Mice via Intestinal Barrier Fortification and Gut Microbiome Modulation.
articles.hook: Omega-3 fatty acids strengthen intestinal barrier in colitis mice
articles.summary: Omega-3 fatty acids improve ulcerative colitis in mice by strengthening the intestinal barrier and modifying gut bacteria.

articles.title: Omega-3 fatty acids in Pediatric Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia: A Scoping Review.
articles.hook: Omega-3 fatty acids show promise in laboratory...
articles.summary: Omega-3 fatty acids show promise in laboratory tests for killing leukemia cells and reducing chemotherapy side effects in children with acute lymphocytic leukemia.

articles.title: Protective effect of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) against prenatal cytarabine exposure-induced developmental toxicity in SD rat.
articles.hook: DHA omega-3 fatty acid protects rat fetuses against cytarabine toxicity
articles.summary: DHA omega-3 fatty acid protects rat fetuses against developmental damage from cytarabine, a blood cancer drug.

articles.title: The relationship between elongation of very long-chain fatty acids (ELOVL) 2 polymorphism rs953413 and blood n-3 HUFA levels: a secondary analysis of EPA treatment in the seAFOod polyp prevention trial.
articles.hook: ELOVL2 rs953413 variant predicts blood omega-3 levels during EPA treatment
articles.summary: A genetic variant (rs953413) affects how individuals absorb and process fish oil supplements, explaining differences in blood omega-3 levels.

articles.title: Omega-3 fatty acids attenuate alterations in penile erectile response by enhancing sexual behavior, nitric oxide-mediated signaling, and penile antioxidant status in tamoxifen-exposed rats.
articles.hook: Omega-3 fatty acids restore erectile function in tamoxifen-treated rats
articles.summary: Omega-3 fatty acids restore sexual function in male rats treated with tamoxifen, a breast cancer drug that impairs erectile response.
